pamphlet_excerpts: Precautions That Must Be Followed: Fingers probably are the most useful tools for working with softclays (p. 19).
Precautions That Must Be Followed Principle 2: You can use a loop tool, a wooden tool with a metal loop on the end, to trim away excess clay (p. 19).

Precautions That Must Be Followed Principle 3: If you are working with soapstone (a soft stone), you will need a rasp and a riffler, ametal tool similar to a rasp with fine, small cutting points (p. 19).
Precautions That Must Be Followed Principle 4: These commercial tools come in handy for the artist working with clay (p. 19).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Precautions That Must Be Followed): Use wood-carving tools, such as rasps, files, gouges, chisels, and V-tools, with great care (p. 19).
Step 2 (Precautions That Must Be Followed): Even though soapstone is quite soft, it still requires a lotof effort to carve a form (p. 19).
Step 3 (Precautions That Must Be Followed): Whenever you see this icon, there will be safety information that goes (p. 19).
Step 4 (Precautions That Must Be Followed): When using knives and chisels to make wood sculptures, always carve and cut away from your body (p. 19).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When carving plaster or soft stone with chisels and rasps, or modeling clay over a wire armature, what studio safety precautions must you take?
quiz_item.question: When carving plaster or soft stone with chisels and rasps, or modeling clay over a wire armature, what studio safety precautions must you take?
options: A. Blow carving dust off your workbench with compressed air and leave wire armature ends unlooped at eye level.
B. Heat vinyl modeling clays in a kitchen oven above 500 degrees Fahrenheit without ventilation to soften them.
C. Wear impact-rated safety goggles when chipping or carving, loop or pad sharp armature wire ends, and clean up plaster or stone dust with a damp sponge or HEPA vacuum rather than dry sweeping.
D. Hold small stone blocks between your knees while striking a cold chisel toward your body.
choices: A. Blow carving dust off your workbench with compressed air and leave wire armature ends unlooped at eye level.
B. Heat vinyl modeling clays in a kitchen oven above 500 degrees Fahrenheit without ventilation to soften them.
C. Wear impact-rated safety goggles when chipping or carving, loop or pad sharp armature wire ends, and clean up plaster or stone dust with a damp sponge or HEPA vacuum rather than dry sweeping.
D. Hold small stone blocks between your knees while striking a cold chisel toward your body.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. Wear impact-rated safety goggles when chipping or carving, loop or pad sharp armature wire ends, and clean up plaster or stone dust with a damp sponge or HEPA vacuum rather than dry sweeping.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Sculpting requires eye protection against flying chips and sharp armature wires, plus wet cleanup and ventilation to avoid inhaling hazardous silica or plaster dust and solvent fumes.

requirements.req_text: Do TWO of the following: (a) Model in clay a life-size human head. Then sculpt in modeling clay, carve in wood or plaster, or use 3D modeling software to make a small-scale model of an animal or person. Explain to your counselor the method and tools you used to sculpt the figure. (b) Make a plaster mold of a fruit or vegetable. In this mold, make a copy of the fruit or vegetable. Explain to your counselor the method and tools you used to make the copy. (c) With your parent or guardian's permission and your counselor's approval, visit a museum, art exhibit, art gallery, artists' co-op, or artist's studio. After your visit, share with your counselor what you have learned. Discuss the importance of visual arts and how it strengthens social tolerance and helps stimulate cultural, intellectual, and personal development.

requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following: (a) Explore careers related to this merit badge. Research one career to learn about the training and education needed, costs, job prospects, salary, job duties, and career advancement. Your research methods may include, with your parent or guardian's permission, an internet or library search, an interview with a professional in the field, or a visit to a location where people in this career work. Discuss with your counselor both your findings and what about this profession might make it an interesting career. Resources: 12 Careers for Sculptors (website) How To Become an Artist/Sculptor (video) Craft Artist Careers (video) (b) Explore how you could use knowledge and skills from this merit badge to pursue a hobby. Research any training needed, expenses, and organizations that promote or support it. Discuss with your counselor what short-term and long-term goals you might have if you pursued this.

pamphlet_excerpts: Careers & Professional Pathways: If you want to pursue a career as aprofessional sculptor, you will need some studio lessons and hands-on training (p. 59).

Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 2: You can start by findingout if your high school offers shop classes that will introduce you to the techniques for working with metal, wood, and plastics (p. 59).
Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 3: Later, you can get hands-on training by working for another artist as an apprentice or assistant (p. 59).
Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 4: If you intend to supplement your income in a related field, you might have to earn advanced degrees (p. 59).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Careers & Professional Pathways): Colleges and universities offer four- and five-year programs that lead to bachelor of fine arts (BFA) or master of fine arts (MFA) degrees (p. 59).
Step 2 (Careers & Professional Pathways): Beyond the core courses common to all major areas of study, these programs include art history and studio art classes (p. 59).
Step 3 (Careers & Professional Pathways): Independent schools of art and design offer two-year programs that lead to an associate of arts or bachelor of fine arts degree (p. 59).
Step 4 (Careers & Professional Pathways): Anyone who wants to teach art in public schools must have a bachelor's degree; you might also need a teaching certificate (p. 59).

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: When carving plaster or soft stone with chisels and rasps, or modeling clay over a wire armature, what studio safety precautions must you take?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: When carving plaster or soft stone with chisels and rasps, or modeling clay over a wire armature, what studio safety precautions must you take?
options: A. Blow carving dust off your workbench with compressed air and leave wire armature ends unlooped at eye level.
B. Heat vinyl modeling clays in a kitchen oven above 500 degrees Fahrenheit without ventilation to soften them.
C. Wear impact-rated safety goggles when chipping or carving, loop or pad sharp armature wire ends, and clean up plaster or stone dust with a damp sponge or HEPA vacuum rather than dry sweeping.
D. Hold small stone blocks between your knees while striking a cold chisel toward your body.
choices: A. Blow carving dust off your workbench with compressed air and leave wire armature ends unlooped at eye level.

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Wear impact-rated safety goggles when chipping or carving, loop or pad sharp armature wire ends, and clean up plaster or stone dust with a damp sponge or HEPA vacuum rather than dry sweeping.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Sculpting requires eye protection against flying chips and sharp armature wires, plus wet cleanup and ventilation to avoid inhaling hazardous silica or plaster dust and solvent fumes.
